external_claims.claim: Electric Hydrogen raised $380 million in a funding round announced October 3, 2023, led by Fortescue, Fifth Wall and Energy Impact Partners.

New investors in Electric Hydrogen's $380 million round included bp Ventures and Oman Investment Authority, alongside existing investors Amazon's Climate Pledge Fund, Equinor Ventures, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Rio Tinto and Breakthrough Energy Ventures.
Electric Hydrogen has raised a cumulative total of approximately $545.57 million to date across its funding history.
As of a 2024 Crunchbase News report, at least 23 hydrogen-focused startups globally had secured financing that year, totaling over $1.4 billion in equity funding.
Ohmium, an electrolyzer maker headquartered in California but manufacturing in India, raised $250 million in its Series C round (reported February 2024).
ZeroAvia was targeting a $150 million funding round as of May 2025 to progress toward commercial introduction of its first hydrogen-powered aircraft technology.
John Cockerill is identified as a leader in high-pressure alkaline electrolyzers with a large global manufacturing footprint.
thyssenkrupp nucera is described as a German-based major manufacturer specializing in electrolyzer technology.
Nel Hydrogen announced a partnership with Ørsted on January 19, 2024 to supply a 20 MW PEM electrolyzer for a green hydrogen production facility.
The U.S. Treasury Department released final rules for the Section 45V Clean Hydrogen Production Tax Credit on January 3, 2025.

Under the finalized Section 45V rules, the tax credit is worth 60 cents per kilogram of hydrogen produced, multiplied by an applicable emissions rate, with different emissions-intensity tiers determining the final credit amount.
The Federal Register notice on the 45V clean hydrogen credit confirms provisions beginning in 2026 for emissions occurring in calendar year 2026 and after.
Between 2020 and 2026, PEM electrolyzer CAPEX fell from roughly $1,200-$1,500 per kW down to about $700-$1,000 per kW.

The U.S. Department of Energy has set an interim cost target of $2/kg for clean hydrogen by 2026, en route to a longer-term $1/kg goal, with electrolyzer system costs targeted to drop to the $250 range per kW.

As of a LinkedIn-referenced industry report roughly 7 months prior to August 2026, rising electrolyzer system costs — often exceeding $1,000 per kilowatt — are cited as creating financial hurdles for green hydrogen developments worldwide, indicating cost declines have stalled or reversed for some project types.

Lhyfe and industrial gas company Messer signed a 10-year hydrogen supply contract, announced July 13, 2026, with Messer taking a 30 percent equity stake in four of Lhyfe's renewable hydrogen production sites.
Mitsubishi Gas Chemical and ACME Group signed a green hydrogen/ammonia-related agreement announced July 3, 2026, tied to ACME's integrated green hydrogen and ammonia project.
BP cancelled its gigascale Duqm Green Hydrogen Project in Oman, confirmed in a Hydrogen Insight report published December 3, 2025.
The cancelled Duqm Green Hydrogen Project in Oman was a 1.5GW facility that was designed to produce 150,000 tonnes of hydrogen annually.

Oman's state hydrogen body Hydrom confirmed BP's exit from the Duqm project alongside the cancellation of a second Omani hydrogen initiative, describing it as a mutually agreed decision, per a December 8, 2025 statement.
Air Products cancelled its planned green hydrogen plant in Massena, New York (designed to produce 35 tons/day of green hydrogen) in February 2025.
A Reuters report dated July 23, 2025 found that green hydrogen developers globally have scaled back investments and scrapped projects due to elevated production costs and weak demand.
Despite high-profile project delays, global investment in clean hydrogen technologies was projected (as of a June 6, 2025 report) to jump 70% in 2025 to almost $8 billion.
